The ability to overlap the thumb and fifth finger is a feature often associated with hypermobile joints, common in genetic disorders with marfanoid features, which distinguishes it from connective tissue disorders without such prominent joint hypermobility.

The presence of hyperelastic skin is more characteristic of Marfanoid features and Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, which are part of the Genetic Disorder with Marfanoid Features branch, than of the Multisystem Developmental Disorder branch.

The developmental milestone of speaking in 2-word phrases at the age of 4 is more consistent with the genetic disorder with marfanoid features in B1, which may have developmental delays but typically not as severe as those seen in multisystem developmental disorders like B3.
